newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer says nations must earn place in EMU.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer says nations must earn place in EMU.

text.p: Europe's single currency would gain from having as many fully-qualified members as possible, but there can be no concessions made to draw more members in, Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said on Thursday.

"Every country which fills all the criteria and is prepared to accept the consequences of the common currency will be an asset to monetary union," Tietmeyer said according to the text of a speech to be delivered in Florence, Italy.
He added, "But almost all countries still have considerable efforts to make. The Maastricht Treaty rightly does not offer concessions to founder members."

Countries which want to meld their currencies in a single currency from 1999 must meet certain economic targets next year. Most of the European Union's 15 members are finding difficulty in reaching the fiscal targets in the Treaty.

Tietmeyer noted that Germany also was not in the clear on this. "The public deficit is clearly above three percent in 1995 and 1996," he said. "That means Germany clearly failed to meet the Maastricht qualification in those two years."
He added that Italy also had work to do, but welcomed the return of the lira to the Exchange Rate Mechanism of the European Monetary System, agreed last weekend.
"The lira is very welcome," he said. "Germany, incidentally, would have been happy to see the lira remaining in the exchange rate mechanism in autumn 1992. But Italy decided differently."
Italy withdrew its currency from the ERM in 1992 after strong speculative pressure.
